name: Muhammad II of Khwarazm
extract: 'Alā' al-Din Muhammad II (Persian: علاءالدین محمد خوارزمشاه; full name: Ala ad-Dunya wa ad-Din Abul-Fath Muhammad Sanjar ibn Tekish) was the Shah of the Khwarazmian Empire from 3 August 1200 to December 1220. His ancestor was Anushtegin Gharchai, a Turkic Ghulam who eventually became a viceroy of a small province in Central Asia named Khwarazm. The expansion seen under the rule of Muhammad encapsulated the pinnacle of Khwarazmian military culture, and in various campaigns of conquest created a realm extending from Shirvan to the Indus river and the outer periphery of Mongolia after defeating his adversaries, namely the Qara Khitai, Ghurids, and Eldiguzids. He was able to rally as much as 400,000 men, and with these massive tribal armies his empire was as large as 3,600,000 square kilometers. By 1218, he brought the empire to its' political and military zenith, but after a skirmish with the mongols, Muhammad's realm was destroyed when they entered into Transoxiana and sacked Gurganj, Bukhara, his capital in Samarkand, Otrar, Herat among others. Muhammad died on an island in the Caspian sea and all of his progress was reversed just before his death.
